title: Travelling salesman (Held–Karp)
statement: Given a symmetric distance matrix for n ≤ 13 cities, return the length of the shortest tour starting and ending at city 0 that visits every city exactly once.
hints: Brute force: (n − 1)! orders, about 4.8 × 10⁸ for n = 13.
dp[mask][v] = the shortest path from 0 visiting exactly mask, ending at v.

solution.explanation: Held–Karp: the future of a partial tour depends only on which cities are visited and where you are, not the order. That collapses (n − 1)! orders to n·2ⁿ states. It's the canonical bitmask DP, and the cleanest example of "the state is what the future needs to know".
